sources.title: flock(2) — Linux manual page
sources.claim: flock locks are advisory and associated with an open file description; descriptors duplicated by fork/dup share the same lock; the lock is released only by explicit unlock or after all duplicates close.
sources.architecture_impact: Add a crash/recovery discriminator in which a forked child survives the parent and retains Frank's physical execution lock. Treat resulting residual BUSY as an availability/recovery failure, not proof of two-active overlap.

sources.title: fork(2) — Linux manual page
sources.claim: Linux fork children inherit copies of the parent's file descriptors and inherit flock locks/open-file-description locks.
sources.architecture_impact: Physical-exclusion recovery tests must include fork inheritance; parent death alone is insufficient to prove lock release.

sources.title: Python 3.14 os documentation
sources.claim: Python file descriptors are non-inheritable for exec by default, but non-inheritable descriptors are still inherited by os.fork().
sources.architecture_impact: Do not assume Python's default non-inheritable flag eliminates fork-retained flock risk.

sources.title: Google Calendar — Create events
sources.claim: Calendar permits a caller-selected event ID and documents that doing so prevents duplicate event creation when an operation fails after successful backend execution.
sources.architecture_impact: Calendar create is a candidate for SAME_KEY_RETRY_SAFE semantics only when Frank deliberately binds a stable provider-valid event ID to the effect attempt and verifies provider behavior.

sources.title: Gmail API — users.messages.send
sources.claim: The send method is POST with userId plus a Message request body; the method reference exposes no client idempotency-key parameter analogous to Calendar's caller-selected event ID.
sources.architecture_impact: Do not mark Gmail send SAME_KEY_RETRY_SAFE from API shape alone. Timeout/transport loss after possible acceptance remains RECONCILE_REQUIRED unless a separately validated reconciliation strategy is available. This is a conservative inference from the primary method contract, not a proof that duplicates are universally unavoidable.

counterevidence_or_limits: flock is advisory, so correctness still depends on every Frank execution entry path cooperating with the gate.
Calendar caller-supplied IDs prevent duplicate create for that API pattern but do not generalize to all providers/actions.
Absence of a Gmail idempotency-key parameter in the method reference is not a universal impossibility proof; it just forbids promoting same-key retry safety without additional evidence.
